transcript.content: Hello, please have a seat. What brings you into the clinic today?

Thank you, Doctor. I really appreciate you seeing me. Um, I hope I'm not wasting your time, I just... well, I want to make sure I'm doing the right thing by being here. 

It's a little embarrassing to talk about, to be honest, because I don't want you to think poorly of me. But... I've been hearing things. Very clear voices. Mostly just in my apartment, or sometimes when I'm out at a museum and happen to be in an empty room. It sounds like... like women whispering from right behind the walls. They tell me which photographs belong in the archive. 

I know how strange that must sound, I'm so sorry. Does... does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining it okay for you.
How long have you been hearing these voices?

Oh, um... well, I really hope it's not too much of a bother that I let it go on this long before coming in. I didn't want to be a nuisance to anyone, so I tried to just handle it myself at first. 

But I suppose it's been... probably about eight months now. That I've been hearing them, I mean. And along with the whispering, I've just had this... this absolute certainty that people are watching my archive. 

I'm so sorry, I know that probably sounds incredibly silly to you. I hope waiting eight months to tell a doctor doesn't make me a terrible patient... am I giving you the right kind of information? I just want to make sure I'm answering your questions properly.
Over these past eight months, how has your mood been overall—have you been feeling down, depressed, or unable to enjoy things?

Oh, well... I really hope I don't sound ungrateful for my life or anything, because I know I have a lot to be thankful for. But... yes, I suppose I have been feeling a bit... flat? 

It's just that there are these long stretches where I'll just sit at my kitchen table. My little herb pots are all drying out because I forget to water them, and... well, I haven't been calling my friends back. Which is terrible of me, I know. Even when they invite me to things I usually love, like a concert or a gallery opening, I just... I don't feel much interest in going. 

I'm sorry, I know that sounds so lazy and antisocial of me. I really am trying to be better about it. Is... is that the kind of thing you were asking about? I hope I'm not complaining too much.
Have there been times over these eight months when you heard the voices even when your mood felt completely fine?

Oh... yes, actually. I hope I'm remembering this right for you, I really want to be as helpful as possible. But there was a period of... well, maybe several weeks, where I actually felt quite normal. I wasn't feeling down at all, and I wasn't feeling especially energized or... or grand, either. Just my regular self. 

But... oh, this is a bit embarrassing to admit, I'm sorry... even when my mood was perfectly fine like that, I still heard the whispers in the apartment. And... well, I was still completely convinced that the arts people were monitoring my phone. 

I hope it's okay that I didn't mention the phone thing earlier, I just... I didn't want you to think I was completely out of my mind. Does that help answer your question? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right details.
Looking back over these past eight months, would you say you felt that low and uninterested feeling for most of the time, or was it only for a small part of it?

Oh, well... I really hope I'm not making things too complicated for you. I want to give you a clear answer, I really do. But... to be completely honest, since I retired, the low feelings haven't actually been the main thing. 

I feel a bit silly saying this, because I know I just went on and on about the herb pots and not calling people back. But for most of these past eight months, it's actually been quite the opposite. I've had these long stretches where I feel... well, incredibly driven. Almost like I've been chosen for something important. I just couldn't seem to slow down, and... I'm so sorry to admit this, but I got quite irritable with people who couldn't keep up with me. 

Even on the days when I felt a bit more withdrawn, that driven, restless feeling was still kind of... running the show, if that makes sense. I hope it's alright that I'm correcting myself like this. I just want to make sure you have the most accurate picture of what's been happening. Am I explaining that clearly enough?
During those times when you felt so driven, did you find yourself needing much less sleep than usual while still feeling full of energy?

Oh, goodness... yes. I hope I don't sound completely unreasonable, but yes, that's exactly what happens. 

I feel a little guilty admitting this, because I know at my age I should be taking better care of myself, getting my full eight hours. But during those times, I'll sleep for maybe... two or three hours? And then I'll wake up well before dawn, and I'm just... completely ready for the day. 

I try to tell myself I should stay in bed, really I do. But I just feel so wide awake, and I end up telling myself that... well, that sleep is just for people who don't have an entire archive to rescue. I know that sounds a bit dramatic, and I'm sorry if it sounds like I'm neglecting my health. I just... I feel so energized, I don't even miss the sleep. Is that... is that very concerning to you? I hope I'm not doing something terribly wrong.
During those stretches when you felt so driven and full of energy, did you also experience feelings of intense sadness or despair at the same time?

Oh... no, I don't believe so. I hope I'm not misunderstanding your question, I really want to be as helpful as I can. But when I was having those stretches of feeling so... so energized and driven, I wasn't sad at all. 

It was actually quite the opposite. I felt very capable, almost... well, too capable, I suppose. But definitely not despairing or down. The low feelings were completely separate from the energetic times. 

I hope it's alright that I didn't have both of those feelings at the exact same time. I know sometimes these things can be so complicated, and I'd hate to be giving you the wrong impression. Does that make sense? I just want to be sure I'm answering you correctly.
